meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'too, also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Me too.
He's here too.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to think', paired with 'подумать'.

examples.trans: I'm thinking about work.
I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.trans: I can't today.
That can't be.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.
Quiet, stop! It really hurts!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to wave, dash off'.

examples.trans: Run away together as a couple.

examples.text: На кухне никто не хочет махнуть без причины.
examples.trans: In the kitchen nobody wants to wave without a reason.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'pair, couple, match' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you.
They are a very handsome couple.

examples.text: Я понимаю, я не пара вам. Вы красавец, а я старая.
examples.trans: I understand I'm no match for you. You're a handsome man, and I'm old.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to mean'.

examples.trans: What does this mean?
So you're not coming.
Pasha, what does all this mean?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'стить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to forgive; (imperative) excuse me', paired with 'прощать'.

examples.trans: Excuse me, who are you?
Forgive me.
Please forgive me.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'fool, silly' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вот я дура! Надо было работать на Осипенко.
examples.trans: What a fool I am! I should have worked for Osipenko.
What a fool I am!

examples.text: Нина, это не моё дело. Но ты дура!
examples.trans: Nina, this is none of my business. But you're being silly!

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.trans: Give me just one.
Some water, please.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'will; freedom, liberty' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Yes, swear on my freedom!
A real head chef requires strong willpower.

examples.text: У меня есть опыт и сильная воля.
examples.trans: I have experience and strong willpower.

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'emotions' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Потому что не умею контролировать свои эмоции!
examples.trans: Because I do not know how to control my emotions!

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть эмоция.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always emotions.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'next; further', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right. Next.
What's next?

examples.text: А дальше? Я очень волнуюсь, я к этому не приспособлена.
examples.trans: And then what? I'm very nervous, I'm not cut out for this.

изменить.gloss: to cheat on, to betray; to change

meanings.en: to cheat on, to betray; to change
meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'менить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to cheat on, to betray; to change', paired with 'изменять'.

examples.trans: Edik, I wanted to cheat on you.
That won't change anything.

examples.text: Эдик, я хотела тебе изменить. С ним, чтобы отомстить.
examples.trans: Edik, I wanted to cheat on you. With him, to take revenge.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'would', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.
Look who's talking.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Too much to do.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, come on, Dad!
Well?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'tyoma' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А вот и мой хороший Тёма!
examples.trans: And here is my good boy Tyoma!
Meet him, please, this is my Tyoma.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крытый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('closed').

examples.trans: I declare the court session closed.
The door was closed.
The loan is closed!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'more; still; yet', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'we will finish talking'.

related.gloss: to we will finish talking (prefixed perfective)
not to we will finish talking (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Тихо, мы с тобой потом договорим.
examples.trans: Quiet, you and I will finish talking later.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и договорить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and we will finish talking on time.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come back, to return', paired with 'возвращаться'.

examples.trans: I'll be back soon.
He came back home.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.
